notes: Summary: Mid-market B2B SaaS (product analytics) evaluating Hosted API for discovery -> moving to Dedicated for predictable economics. Team: CTO (Maya R.), Head of Product (Aaron L.), Platform Eng lead (Rina B.). Primary ask: reduce unit cost for embeddings + chat at production scale while keeping <100ms P99 token latency for chat flows. Hosted POC: good functional fit; observed cost spikes during sustained heavy embedding indexing and occasional tail latency during concurrent batch writes. Decision drivers: cost predictability, VPC networking, audit trail, rollout control. Pricing conversation specifics: they are sensitive to commit sizing — want a three-phase ramp: pilot (1 month, 30% commit), scale (3 months, 70% commit), steady-state (12 month, 100% commit) with defined burst pool for >commit usage. Proposed terms discussed: 12-month dedicated contract with 2 burst classes (short-lived fast-burst with 2x rate limit, and long-burst at lower priority). Overage model options on table: flat per-token overage vs. tiered discounted overage tied to committed capacity. They asked for an example billing simulation for expected usage patterns (see attached drive pricing_v2). Key security asks: SSO/SAML, KMS integration, audit logging retention 1 year, option for EU-only residency for subsets of data. Legal asked to see indemnity language and DB deletion SLA. Procurement constraints: contract requires CFO sign-off for >$200k ARR. AE notes: customer favors Redwood for unified runtime and built-in rollout/A/B features but needs clearer financial predictability than Hosted.
